schema_agreement.title: schema agreement
schema_agreement.description: Both ends were built from compatible schemas, which the handshake checks.

encoding_agreement.title: encoding agreement
encoding_agreement.description: Both ends use the same format and framing, which the handshake checks.

encoding_conformance.title: encoding conformance
encoding_conformance.description: An implementation encodes what its name promises, proven by conformance vectors.

version_honesty.title: version honesty
version_honesty.description: A version bump says what the change breaks, as the version comparison works it out.

bounded_size.title: bounded size
bounded_size.description: Every value has a maximum size, so a decoder refuses an oversized one before allocating it.

struct_fields.title: struct fields
struct_fields.description: How a struct's fields are written.

values.by_position: back to back, in declaration order

unknown_field.title: unknown field
unknown_field.description: What a reader does with a field its type doesn't have.

missing_optional.title: missing optional
missing_optional.description: What a reader does when an optional field isn't there.

enum_variants.title: enum variants
enum_variants.description: How an enum's variant is written.

values.by_index: by its position in the declaration

unknown_variant.title: unknown variant
unknown_variant.description: What a reader does with a variant its type doesn't have.

integer_width.title: integer width
integer_width.description: Whether an integer reads into another width.

values.exact: only the width it was written as

output.title: output
output.description: The grammar a format writes in, which a framing's `payload` must take.

values.bytes: bytes in no grammar a framing reads

calls.title: calls
calls.description: How a request names the function it calls.

values.by_id: by the protocol's and function's wire numbers

directions.title: directions
directions.description: Whether a frame says if it's a request or a response.

values.both: it does, so calls can go both ways on one transport

errors.title: errors
errors.description: How an error response names its error.

values.by_ordinal: by its position in the declaration

payload.title: payload
payload.description: What a framing needs of a payload, which a format's `output` must fit.

values.opaque: any bytes, carried as they are
values.json: JSON text, written into the frame

values.true: it does, and refuses a peer that wasn't

encoding_agreement.title: encoding agreement
encoding_agreement.description: Whether the handshake checks both ends use the same format and framing.

values.true: it does, and refuses a peer that doesn't

packed@1.title: packed
packed@1.description: Fixed-width fields back to back, varint lengths, no tags.

json@1.title: JSON
json@1.description: Values as UTF-8 JSON: a struct as an object.

msgpack@1.title: MessagePack
msgpack@1.description: Values as MessagePack: a struct as an array.

datagram@1.title: datagram
datagram@1.description: Comline's own binary framing of requests and responses.

datagram@2.title: datagram@2
datagram@2.description: The datagram framing with a request/reply kind and a protocol number, for calls both ways and several protocols on one connection.

datagram@3.title: datagram@3
datagram@3.description: The datagram framing that addresses a call by its protocol's and function's wire numbers.

comline@1.title: comline@1
comline@1.description: The fixed frame each end sends first: magic, version, IR hash, wire format, framing and capabilities.

comline@2.title: comline@2
comline@2.description: The compatibility-checking handshake: lines, shape hashes and wire numbers instead of an exact IR match.

none.title: no handshake
none.description: No frame and nothing checked. Unversioned, since there is nothing to evolve; it establishes neither agreement.

name-hash.title: name hash
name-hash.description: FNV-1a 64 of a wire format or framing name, as the handshake carries it

handshake.title: handshake
handshake.description: the fixed 31-byte frame each side sends first: magic, version, IR hash, wire format, framing, capabilities

envelope.title: envelope
envelope.description: a response's outcome: ok with a payload, an error ordinal with its body, or a provider fault

framing-datagram.title: datagram framing
framing-datagram.description: Comline's own binary framing of requests and responses

framing-datagram2.title: datagram@2 framing
framing-datagram2.description: the datagram framing with a request/reply kind and a protocol number, for calls in both directions and several protocols on one connection

framing-datagram3.title: datagram@3 framing
framing-datagram3.description: the datagram framing that addresses a call by its protocol's and function's wire numbers, both varints (calls = by_id); replies as datagram@2

handshake-comline2.title: comline@2 handshake
handshake-comline2.description: the compatibility-checking handshake: its hello, answer and verdict messages, and its negotiation steps under every parameter, with every refusal reason

stream.title: stream framing
stream.description: frames on a byte stream (TCP, a pipe): each behind a u32 little-endian length prefix, refused over the limit, by default 16 MiB (16777216 bytes) in every runtime

framing-jsonrpc.title: JSON-RPC framing
framing-jsonrpc.description: JSON-RPC 2.0 requests and responses, a fault as -32603

format-json.title: JSON wire format
format-json.description: values as UTF-8 JSON: a struct as an object

format-msgpack.title: MessagePack wire format
format-msgpack.description: values as MessagePack: a struct as an array

format-packed.title: packed wire format
format-packed.description: values as packed@1: fixed-width fields back to back, varint lengths, no tags
